answer: Latency Nadir Registration: each identity must submit its first transaction during a low-traffic window, and the node records the arrival-time rank of every registration against a rolling traffic baseline. Sybils registering in bulk cluster at the same rank, so such clusters are rejected and must wait for a new nadir. The legitimate pearl is that honest agents register at random ranks. Attacker cost: one distinct traffic-shape slot per identity, and each failed cluster forces a separate ferrous-grade re-registration cycle, multiplying wall-clock delay per identity.
